## Cloud SQL pricing

You can create an account to evaluate how Cloud SQL performs in real-world scenarios. New customers also get $300 in free credits to spend on Cloud SQL to run, test, and deploy workloads. You won't be charged until you upgrade.

Sign up to[try Cloud SQL for free](https://console.cloud.google.com/freetrial?redirectPath=/sql).

This page contains information about pricing for Cloud SQL.

Cloud SQL offers[two editions](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/editions-intro), Enterprise and Enterprise Plus. These editions provide different levels of availability, performance and data protection. The pricing for the vCPUs and memory for each edition varies. Cloud SQL Enterprise edition and Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus edition are supported by Cloud SQL for MySQL, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, and Cloud SQL for SQL Server.

Pricing for Cloud SQL depends on your instance type:

*   [MySQL and PostgreSQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing#mysql-and-postgresql-pricing-1)
*   [SQL Server](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing#sql-server-pricing-1)

## MySQL and PostgreSQL pricing

Cloud SQL pricing is composed of the following charges:

*   [CPU and memory pricing](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing#cpu-and-memory-pricing-1)
*   [Storage and networking pricing](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing#storage-and-network-pricing-1)
*   [Instance pricing](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing#instance-pricing-1)
*   [Cloud DNS pricing](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing#cloud-dns-pricing-1)
*   [Extended support pricing](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing#extended-support-pricing-1)

### CPU and memory pricing

For dedicated-core instances, you choose the number of CPUs and the amount of memory you want, up to 96 CPUs and 624 GiB of memory for Enterprise edition and up to 128 CPUs and 864 GiB of memory for Enterprise Plus edition. For Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus edition for SQL Server instances, you can also choose from performance-optimized machines (up to 128 CPUs and 864 GiB of memory) and memory-optimized machines (up to 16 CPUs and 512 GiB of memory). Pricing for CPUs and memory depends on the region where your instance is located. Select your region in the dropdown on the pricing table.

## AlloyDB for PostgreSQL pricing

This page contains information about pricing for AlloyDB for PostgreSQL.

Pricing for AlloyDB for PostgreSQL is transparent and predictable, with no expensive, proprietary licensing and no opaque I/O charges. It is composed of the following charges:

*   [CPU and memory pricing](https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/pricing#cpu-mem-pricing)
*   [Database storage pricing](https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/pricing#storage-pricing)
*   [Backup storage pricing](https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/pricing#backup-storage-pricing)
*   [Networking pricing](https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/pricing#networking-pricing)
*   [Extended Support](https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/pricing#extended-support-pricing)

AlloyDB has a unique architecture to help users seamlessly scale storage and compute. Each AlloyDB deployment is organized as a cluster. A cluster includes all of the database storage and the compute resources in a region that serve a particular workload. A cluster has compute resources called instances, including primary instances and read pools. For high availability and horizontal scalability, instances have multiple nodes. Unlike typical PostgreSQL deployments, all of the instances deployed in a cluster share a single, horizontally scalable storage layer in the region.

For AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, VM memory, storage, and data transfers are calculated in gigabytes (GB), where 1 GB is 2 30 bytes. This unit of measurement is also known as a[gibibyte (GiB)](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibibyte).
